01.1Chapter 1 — Machine Learning Systems in Production

Machine Learning kab use karein — aur kab nahi

Machine learning har problem ka jawab nahi hai. Book ki definition ke hisaab se ML ek aisa approach hai jo (1) seekhta hai, (2) complex patterns ko, (3) existing data se, (4) unseen data par predictions karne ke liye. Matlab, agar inme se koi ek condition missing hai, to ML shayad sahi tool nahi hai.

ML use karne ki 6 conditions

  • Learn: system me seekhne ki capacity honi chahiye. Ek relational database ML system nahi hai, kyunki woh seekhta nahi, sirf store karta hai.
  • Complex patterns: pattern itna complex ho ki simple rules se capture na ho sake. Jaise ghar ka kiraya uski location, size, facilities jaise kai factors par depend karta hai.
  • Patterns exist karte hon: agar data me koi pattern hi nahi hai — jaise stock market ke random fluctuations — to ML bhi kuch nahi seekh payega.
  • Existing data: ML data se seekhta hai, isliye data hona ya collect karna possible hona chahiye. Zero-shot learning me bhi model pehle kisi aur data par train hua hota hai.
  • Predictions: ML sirf predictive problems solve karta hai. Agar problem prediction ki nahi hai, to ML fit nahi hoga.
  • Unseen data: training data se seekhe hue patterns unseen data par bhi kaam karne chahiye. Dono ka distribution similar hona chahiye, warna model fail karega.

ML kab khaas taur par useful hai

  • Repetitive kaam: insaan few-shot learning me achha hai, lekin hazaaron baar ek hi kaam dohrane me ML behtar hai.
  • Galat prediction sasti ho: agar ek-do galti se nuksaan nahi hota, to ML chalega. Lekin jahan ek galti catastrophic ho, wahan ML akele kaafi nahi.
  • Scale par ho: ML me upfront investment hoti hai — data, compute, team. Yeh investment tabhi justify hoti hai jab problem scale par ho aur bahut saara data available ho.
  • Patterns badalte rehte hon: culture, taste aur technology badalti rehti hai. Jo pattern aaj kaam karta hai, woh kal badal sakta hai — isliye ML systems ko adapt karna padta hai.

Ek aur important baat: agar simple solution kaam kar jata hai, to ML mat use karo. Simple heuristics ya rules se shuru karo, aur sirf tab ML lao jab woh clearly behtar ho.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 1

01.2Chapter 1 — Machine Learning Systems in Production

ML use cases — enterprise aur consumer

ML aaj har jagah hai — phone me, ghar me, aur bade businesses me. Use cases ko do bade groups me baanta ja sakta hai: consumer applications aur enterprise applications. Dono ke challenges alag hain.

Consumer use cases

  • Machine translation: translation quality me ek hi leap me 10 saal ki progress se zyada sudhaar aaya, jab neural translation systems production me aaye.
  • Smartphone assistants: voice, camera, keyboard suggestions — phone me ML har roz kaam karta hai.
  • Smart home: personal assistants aur smart devices ghar me ML le aaye hain.
  • Consumer apps distribute karna aasan hota hai, lekin unse paise kamana aur users ko retain karna mushkil hota hai.

Enterprise use cases

  • Fraud detection: enterprise me ML ke sabse purane use cases me se ek — galat transactions ko pakadna.
  • Pricing: product ya service ki sahi keemat tay karna business ke liye sabse important decisions me se ek hai.
  • Demand forecasting: customer demand predict karke inventory aur supply plan karna.
  • Customer acquisition aur churn: naya user laana mehenga hota hai, isliye existing customers ko khush rakhna aur unke chhodne ke signals pehchanana zaroori hai.
  • Brand monitoring: log brand ke baare me kya keh rahe hain, yeh track karna.
  • Healthcare, transport, farming: abhi bhi kai naye use cases explore hone baaki hain.

Enterprise ML me data zyada structured hota hai aur ROI measure karna aasan hota hai, lekin deployment ke challenges — reliability, compliance, scale — zyada bade hote hain.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 1

01.3Chapter 1 — Machine Learning Systems in Production

Mind vs Data — kaun jeetega?

ML me ek purani behes hai: kya success intelligent algorithms (mind) se aati hai ya massive data (data) se? Dono camps ke apne strong arguments hain, aur yeh behes aaj bhi chal rahi hai.

Mind over data camp

Is camp ka kehna hai ki sirf data kaafi nahi — system ko duniya ka causal structure samajhna chahiye. Sirf correlations seekhne se model galat conclusions par pahunch sakta hai, khaas taur par jab data biased ho. Inka argument hai ki human-like reasoning aur causal understanding ke bina ML aage nahi badh sakta.

Data over mind camp

Doosra camp kehta hai ki compute aur data badhne ke saath simple methods bhi jeet jaate hain. Ek mashhoor essay ka argument hai ki lambe samay me wahi methods jeet te hain jo zyada computation aur data ka fayda uthate hain. Search ke ek senior leader ne bhi kaha tha ki unki search itni achhi isliye hai kyunki unke paas bahut zyada data hai.

Data science hierarchy of needs

Ek data leader ne hierarchy di thi: sabse pehle data collect karo, phir usko move aur store karo, phir explore aur transform karo, phir aggregate aur label karo, aur uske baad hi ML aur deep learning ki baari aati hai. Matlab, fancy models se pehle data foundation strong hona chahiye.

Asliyat yeh hai ki debate "data zaroori hai ya nahi" ki nahi hai — data to zaroori hai hi. Asli sawal yeh hai ki kya finite data kaafi hai, ya hamesha aur data chahiye hoga. Language models ke datasets ka size log scale par tezi se badha hai, jo data camp ki jeet dikhata hai. Lekin production me sirf data kaafi nahi hota — wahan data ke saath engineering, monitoring aur samajh bhi chahiye.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 1

01.4Chapter 1 — Machine Learning Systems in Production

Research vs Production — duniya kitni alag hai

Research me jo kaam karta hai, woh production me aksar fail ho jata hai. Iski wajah yeh hai ki research aur production ki duniya bilkul alag hai — data, requirements, stakeholders, sab kuch.

Data ka farq

  • Research: data clean, static aur mostly historical hota hai. Benchmarks ke liye datasets fix rehte hain, aur processing scripts open-source mil jate hain.
  • Production: data messy hai, constantly shift hota hai, aur historical ke saath streaming data bhi aata hai. Privacy aur regulatory concerns bhi hote hain.

Stakeholders aur requirements

Research project me sabka goal ek hota hai — leaderboard par achha score. Production me ML engineers, sales team, product managers, platform team aur managers — sabke goals alag hote hain. ML engineer accuracy chahta hai, sales team profitable recommendations chahti hai, product team latency girne se pareshan hoti hai, aur manager margin maximize karna chahta hai.

Ek example: ek model thoda accurate hai lekin slow hai, doosra thoda kam accurate lekin fast hai. Kaunsa choose karein? Yeh sirf accuracy ka sawal nahi hai — latency requirement hard hai ya nice-to-have, is par depend karta hai. Agar latency limit cross ho gayi to users app band kar denge, to dono models bekaar hain.

Leaderboards ki problem

Leaderboards par hard steps — data cleaning, deployment, monitoring — skip kar diye jate hain. Multiple-hypothesis testing ki wajah se bhi leaderboard winners hamesha real-world me best nahi hote. Isliye research results ko production success samajhna galti hai.

Fairness aur interpretability

Research me fairness aur interpretability "good to have" hote hain, production me yeh important hain. Model real logon par use hota hai, isliye biased predictions ka asar real hota hai — ML future predict nahi karta, past ko encode karta hai, aur past ke biases ko aage badha sakta hai. Interpretability bhi zaroori hai: ek aisa system jo explain na kar sake, use log bharosa nahi karenge, khaas taur par healthcare jaise domains me.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 1
← PichhlaMind vs Data — kaun jeetega?Agla →Latency vs Throughput — aur percentiles kyun matter karte hain
01.5Chapter 1 — Machine Learning Systems in Production

Latency vs Throughput — aur percentiles kyun matter karte hain

Research me throughput matter karta hai — ek time me kitne samples process kar sakte ho. Production me latency matter karti hai — ek query ka jawab kitni jaldi milega. Dono ek hi cheez nahi hain, aur inke beech tradeoff hota hai.

Definitions

  • Latency: ek query ko process karne me kitna time laga. Jaise 10ms latency ka matlab hai ek query 10ms me process hoti hai.
  • Throughput: ek specific time me kitni queries process hui. Agar har query 10ms leti hai aur queries ek-ek karke process hoti hain, to throughput 100 queries/second hoga.

Modern distributed systems queries ko batch karke process karte hain, isliye latency aur throughput ka relation simple nahi rehta. Batching se throughput badhta hai, lekin individual query ko batch bharne ka wait karna padta hai, jisse latency badh sakti hai.

Average kyun kaafi nahi — percentiles dekho

Average latency misleading ho sakti hai. Example: 10 requests me se 9 requests 100ms me aur ek request 3000ms me complete hui, to average 390ms hoga — lekin ek user ko 3 second wait karna pada. Isliye percentiles use karo: p95, p99 jaise metrics batate hain ki sabse slow 5% ya 1% users ko kaisa experience mila.

High percentiles outliers ko pakadne me bhi madad karte hain, aur aksar SLAs high percentiles par define kiye jate hain — jaise "p99 latency 200ms se kam honi chahiye". Latency kam karne se throughput bhi kam ho sakta hai, isliye dono ko saath me dekhna zaroori hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 1

01.6Chapter 1 — Machine Learning Systems in Production

ML systems vs traditional software

ML software engineering ka hissa hai, lekin ML systems traditional software se kaafi alag hote hain. Traditional software sirf code hota hai; ML system code + data + artifacts ka combination hota hai.

Teen cheezein version karni padti hain

Traditional software me sirf code test aur version karna padta hai. ML me code ke saath data aur model artifacts (weights, configs) bhi version karne padte hain, kyunki data badalte hi model ka behaviour badal jata hai. Data fast change hota hai, isliye ML applications ko adaptive hona padta hai.

Silent failures

Traditional software me failure par warning milti hai — crash, error message. ML system me failure silent hoti hai: model galat predictions dene lagta hai, lekin system chalta rehta hai. End users ko pata bhi nahi chalta ki system fail ho gaya hai. Isliye monitoring ML me aur bhi zaroori hai.

Data poisoning

ML systems par ek unique attack hai — data poisoning. Attacker training data me malicious examples daal kar model ko poison kar sakta hai. Example: face recognition system ko aise train kar diya jaye ki woh kisi khaas chehre ko pehchan na paye ya galat pehchane. Traditional software me aisa attack vector nahi hota.

Bade models ki challenge

Models ka size bahut bada ho gaya hai — kuch models GBs ke hote hain. Inko production me, khaas taur par edge devices par, chalana ek engineering challenge hai. Model ke complex hone ke saath uske andar kya ho raha hai, yeh dekhna bhi mushkil ho jata hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 1

01.7Chapter 1 — Machine Learning Systems in Production

ML system design — 4 requirements aur iterative process

ML systems design ka matlab hai ML system ke saare components ko define karna — sirf algorithm nahi, balki interface, data stack, hardware aur infrastructure bhi. System banane se pehle uski requirements define karna zaroori hai.

4 requirements

  • Reliability: system ko sahi function, desired level par, continue karna chahiye. ML me reliability mushkil hai kyunki failures silent hote hain.
  • Scalability: system kai tareekon se grow kar sakta hai — traffic volume, data volume, ya model count. Shuru me ek model hota hai, baad me har country ya har customer segment ke liye alag model ho sakta hai. Peak par 100 GPUs chahiye ho sakte hain, lekin zyada time kam chahiye — isliye autoscaling important hai. Growth sirf resources ka sawal nahi, artifacts ka bhi hai.
  • Maintainability: ML system par kai log kaam karte hain. Jab problem aaye, to alag contributors apne hisse par independently kaam kar sakein — isliye code, data aur models ko clean aur documented rakhna chahiye.
  • Adaptability: data distributions aur business requirements badalte rehte hain, isliye system ko jaldi evolve karna chahiye. Yeh continual learning se juda hai.

Iterative process — 6 steps

ML system banana linear process nahi hai, yeh ek cycle hai jisme bahut back-and-forth hota hai:

  1. Project scoping: goals, objectives aur resources estimate karo.
  2. Data engineering: data collect, clean aur manage karo — zyada tar models data se seekhte hain.
  3. ML model development: features extract karo, model train karo, evaluate karo.
  4. Deployment: model ko production me le jao.
  5. Monitoring aur continual learning: production me performance monitor karo aur naye data se update karo.
  6. Business analysis: model performance ko business goals se compare karo — aur phir wapas step 1 par jao.

Jaise likhna kabhi khatm nahi hota, waise hi ML system kabhi "complete" nahi hota — yeh hamesha evolve karta rehta hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 1
