02.1Chapter 2 — Data Engineering Fundamentals

Data sources — data aata kahan se hai

ML systems data se seekhte hain, isliye pehla sawal yeh hai: data aata kahan se hai? Book 4 bade sources batati hai, aur har source ki apni nature aur challenges hain.

User input data

Yeh woh data hai jo users khud daalte hain — text, images, videos, uploaded files. Users se galti hoti hi hai: text bahut lamba ya chhota ho sakta hai, numbers ki jagah text aa sakta hai, galat format ki file upload ho sakti hai. Isliye user input ko heavy checking aur processing chahiye. Users ko turant result bhi chahiye hota hai, isliye is data ki processing fast honi chahiye.

System-generated data

  • Logs: system ki state aur important events record karte hain — memory usage, kaunsi services call hui, jobs ke results. Debugging ke liye logs essential hain, lekin volume bahut fast badhta hai aur signals noise me kho jate hain. Logs ko sirf utne time store karo jitne time woh useful hon.
  • User behaviour data: clicks, choices, scrolling, popup ignore karna — yeh system-generated hai lekin user data mana jata hai aur privacy regulations ke under aata hai. Yeh future models ko train karne ke kaam bhi aata hai.

Internal databases

Company ke alag services aur enterprise applications apne databases banate hain — inventory, customer relationship, users. ML models inhe directly use kar sakte hain. Example: search query par ML model intent detect karta hai, phir internal database se product availability check ki jati hai.

First, second aur third-party data

  • First-party: jo data aapki company khud apne users ke baare me collect karti hai.
  • Second-party: doosri company ka data jo woh aapko deti hai, aksar paise lekar.
  • Third-party: woh companies jo un logon ka data collect karti hain jo unke customers nahi hain — social media activity, purchase history, browsing habits. Yeh data structured aur cleaned milta hai, lekin privacy concerns bahut hain.

Smartphones ke unique advertiser IDs se third-party data collect karna aasan tha, lekin privacy demands badhne par — jaise ek bade phone maker ne apna advertiser ID opt-in kar diya — third-party data kam ho gaya hai, aur companies first-party data par focus karne lagi hain.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaML system design — 4 requirements aur iterative processAgla →Data formats aur serialization — JSON se Parquet tak
02.2Chapter 2 — Data Engineering Fundamentals

Data formats aur serialization — JSON se Parquet tak

Data milne ke baad use store karna padta hai. Format choose karte time sochna chahiye: data kaise use hoga, multimodal data (image + text) kaise store hoga, cheap aur fast access kaise milega, aur models alag hardware par kaise load honge.

Serialization kya hai

Data structure ko aise format me convert karna jise store ya transmit kiya ja sake aur baad me wapas reconstruct kiya ja sake — yahi serialization hai. Format choose karte time human readability, access pattern aur text vs binary nature dekho.

Common formats

  • JSON: text, human-readable, har jagah use hota hai. Key-value pairs simple lekin powerful hain, nested data bhi handle kar lete hain.
  • CSV: text, human-readable, har jagah use hota hai, lekin types aur nesting ke liye weak hai.
  • Parquet: binary, column-major format. Book ka example: ek 14MB CSV file Parquet me sirf 6MB ki ho gayi. Hadoop aur data warehouses me use hota hai.
  • Avro: binary, Hadoop ecosystem me use hota hai.
  • Protobuf: binary, ek bade tech company aur ek ML framework ke record format me use hota hai.
  • Pickle: binary, Python-specific serialization.

Row-major vs column-major

Row-major format me ek row ke saare columns saath store hote hain — row-wise access fast hoti hai. Column-major me ek column ke saare values saath store hote hain — column-wise access aur compression fast hoti hai. Ek experiment me DataFrame ko column-wise iterate karna 0.07 seconds me hua, lekin row-wise iterate karna bahut slow tha; NumPy array me convert karne par row access fast ho gayi. Isliye access pattern dekh kar format choose karo.

Text vs binary

Text formats human-readable hote hain aur debug karna aasan hota hai, lekin file size bada hota hai. Binary formats compact hote hain aur fast parse hote hain, lekin human-readable nahi hote. ML me large datasets ke liye binary columnar formats aksar behtar hote hain.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaData sources — data aata kahan se haiAgla →Data models — relational, document aur graph
02.3Chapter 2 — Data Engineering Fundamentals

Data models — relational, document aur graph

Data model yeh define karta hai ki data ko kaise represent aur organise kiya jaye. Alag use cases ke liye alag models fit hote hain.

Relational model

Relational model me data tables (relations) me hota hai. Har relation me rows aur columns hote hain, aur rows ya columns ka order matter nahi karta. Data ko normalize karke alag tables me baanta jata hai taaki duplication kam ho. Example: books ki information ko book table aur publisher table me alag karna, taaki publisher ka naam har row me repeat na ho.

NoSQL — document model

Document model me data JSON jaise documents me store hota hai. Ek book ka saara data — title, author, publisher — ek hi document me aa sakta hai. Yeh flexible hai, schema change karna aasan hai, aur nested data ke liye achha hai. Lekin joins aur complex queries relational se mushkil ho sakte hain.

Graph model

Graph model me data nodes aur unke beech relationships (edges) ke roop me hota hai. Yeh un use cases ke liye best hai jahan relationships hi main hain — jaise social networks, recommendation systems, ya knowledge graphs.

Structured vs unstructured data

Structured data ka clear schema hota hai — search aur analyze karna aasan hai. Unstructured data — text, images, video — ka koi fixed schema nahi hota, lekin yeh fast arrive karta hai aur volume bahut bada hota hai. Aaj kal zyada tar ML data unstructured ya semi-structured hota hai.

Ek model choose karte time yeh dekho: data ka structure kya hai, queries kaisi hongi, aur scale kya hai. Galat model choose karne se baad me migration bahut mehenga padta hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaData formats aur serialization — JSON se Parquet takAgla →Storage engines — warehouses, lakes aur lakehouse
02.4Chapter 2 — Data Engineering Fundamentals

Storage engines — warehouses, lakes aur lakehouse

Data kahan store karein — yeh decision access pattern aur use case par depend karta hai. Teen bade options hain: data warehouses, data lakes, aur unka hybrid — lakehouse.

Transactional vs analytical processing

OLTP (transactional) systems fast, small operations ke liye hote hain — jaise ek order place karna. OLAP (analytical) systems bade aggregates aur analysis ke liye hote hain — jaise pichhle saal ki sales ka trend nikalna. Book kehti hai ki 2021 tak yeh terms outdated hone lage the, kyunki modern systems dono kaam karne lage hain.

Data warehouses

Warehouses me structured data predefined schema ke saath store hota hai. Search aur analysis fast hoti hai, lekin data daalne se pehle schema fix karna padta hai, jo slow aur rigid ho sakta hai.

Data lakes

Lakes me raw data bina schema ke store hota hai — koi bhi format, koi bhi volume. Data fast arrive karta hai, kyunki pehle processing nahi karni padti. Lekin bade raw data me se chahiye hua piece dhoondhna inefficient ho jata hai, aur lake jaldi "data swamp" ban sakta hai.

Lakehouse

Companies ne hybrid solutions banaye jo lakes ki flexibility aur warehouses ki management dono dete hain. Is approach me data lake me store hota hai, lekin us par warehouse jaisi management aur query capabilities milti hain.

Rule of thumb: agar tumhe pata hai ki data kaise query hoga aur schema stable hai, to warehouse achha hai. Agar data diverse hai aur schema evolve ho raha hai, to lake ya lakehouse socho.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaData models — relational, document aur graphAgla →ETL aur ELT — data ko shape me laana
02.5Chapter 2 — Data Engineering Fundamentals

ETL aur ELT — data ko shape me laana

Raw data seedha model me nahi daala ja sakta. Use pehle extract, transform aur load karna padta hai — yahi ETL hai. Yeh data layer ki underlying structure hai kai organizations me.

ETL ke 3 steps

  • Extract: data sources se chahiye hua data nikalo. Data multiple sources se, alag formats me aayega, kuch corrupted bhi hoga. Is phase me data validate karo aur requirements meet na karne wale data ko reject karo. Pehle step me sahi karna downstream me bahut time bachata hai.
  • Transform: yeh sabse meaty hissa hai — data ko clean karo, multiple sources ko join karo, value ranges standardize karo (jaise ek source "Male/Female" likhta hai, doosra "M/F" ya "1/2"), deduplicate karo, sort karo, aggregate karo, naye features derive karo.
  • Load: transformed data ko target destination — file, database ya warehouse — me kaise aur kitni baar load karna hai, yeh decide karo.

ELT — ulta order

Jab data ka volume aur sources bahut badh gaye, to companies ne socha: pehle saara data lake me load kar do, processing baad me kar lenge. Yeh ELT hai (Extract, Load, Transform). Isse data fast arrive karta hai, kyunki store karne se pehle processing nahi karni padti.

Lekin jaise-jaise data badhta hai, raw data me search karna inefficient ho jata hai. Cloud aur standardized infrastructure ke saath schemas bhi standardize hone lage, aur predefined schema par commit karna feasible ho gaya. Isliye aaj kai teams ETL aur ELT dono ka mix use karti hain — use case ke hisaab se.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaStorage engines — warehouses, lakes aur lakehouseAgla →Modes of dataflow — databases, services aur real-time transport
02.6Chapter 2 — Data Engineering Fundamentals

Modes of dataflow — databases, services aur real-time transport

Production me ek process nahi, kai processes hote hain. Sawal yeh hai: ek process se doosre process tak data kaise pahunche, jab woh memory share nahi karte? Dataflow ke 3 main modes hain.

1. Data passing through databases

Sabse aasan tareeka: process A database me likhe, process B wahan se padhe. Lekin isme 2 problems hain — dono processes ko same database ki access chahiye (alag companies ke processes ke liye mushkil), aur database read/write slow hota hai, jo strict latency wale apps ke liye suitable nahi hai.

2. Data passing through services

Ek process doosre ko network par request bhejta hai — REST ya RPC APIs ke through. Yeh request-driven architecture hai. Isse microservice architecture banti hai: har component alag service hota hai, jo independently develop, test aur maintain kiya ja sakta hai.

Example: ride-sharing app me 3 services — driver management (kitne drivers available honge), ride management (kitni rides request hongi), aur price optimization (sahi kiraya kya ho). Price service ko dono se data chahiye, isliye woh har ride request par unse data mangta hai. REST public APIs ke liye predominant hai, jabki RPC zyada tar same organization ke services ke beech use hota hai.

Request-driven passing synchronous hoti hai: agar ek service down hai, to us par depend karne wali services bhi atak jati hain, aur response lost ho sakta hai.

3. Data passing through real-time transport

Jab services ki sankhya badhti hai, to har service ka har doosri service se request karna ek jaal ban jata hai. Solution: ek broker beech me rakh do. Har service apna data broker ko broadcast karti hai, aur jise chahiye woh broker se padh leta hai. Har service ko sirf broker se baat karni padti hai.

Broker par broadcast kiya gaya data piece ek event kehlata hai — isliye yeh event-driven architecture hai. Do common types hain: pubsub (publish-subscribe — koi bhi topic par publish kar sakta hai, subscribers saare events padhte hain; data kuch din retain rehta hai phir delete ya permanent storage me move hota hai) aur message queue (har message ke intended consumers hote hain, aur queue message ko sahi consumer tak pahunchata hai). Pubsub ke examples hain ek popular open-source streaming platform aur ek cloud streaming service; message queues ke examples hain do popular queue systems. Request-driven architecture logic-heavy systems ke liye achha hai, event-driven data-heavy systems ke liye.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaETL aur ELT — data ko shape me laanaAgla →Batch processing vs stream processing
02.7Chapter 2 — Data Engineering Fundamentals

Batch processing vs stream processing

Data storage me pahunchne ke baad woh historical data ban jata hai. Jo data abhi aa raha hai, woh streaming data hai. Dono ki processing alag tareeke se hoti hai.

Batch processing

Historical data ko batch jobs me process kiya jata hai — jobs jo periodically chalte hain, jaise roz ek baar pichhle din ki saari rides ka average surge charge compute karna. Batch processing par decades se research ho rahi hai, aur distributed systems jaise ek early map-reduce framework aur ek popular distributed engine iske liye banaye gaye hain.

Stream processing

Real-time transports me jo data hai, use stream processing se handle kiya jata hai — data aate hi process karo, wait mat karo. Streaming me latency low hoti hai, lekin system ko hamesha on rehna padta hai aur failures ko handle karna padta hai.

Kaunsa kab choose karein

  • Batch: jab result turant nahi chahiye — daily reports, model training, large aggregates.
  • Stream: jab real-time response chahiye — fraud detection, live recommendations, monitoring alerts.

ML systems me dono ki zaroorat padti hai: training ke liye batch data, aur online predictions ke liye streaming data. Aage ke chapters me dekhenge ki in dono pipelines ko unify karna kyun mushkil aur zaroori hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaModes of dataflow — databases, services aur real-time transportAgla →Sampling — sahi data chunna
03.1Chapter 3 — Training Data

Sampling — sahi data chunna

Training data banana ek iterative process hai. Pehla sawal: poora data use karein ya sample lein? Real-world data itna bada hota hai ki aksar poora data use karna possible ya zaroori nahi hota. Sahi sampling se model fast train hota hai aur phir bhi representative rehta hai.

Non-probability sampling

Isme samples ko kisi fixed probability ke bina chuna jata hai — jaise jo data aasani se mil gaya woh le liya, ya experts ne jo samples choose kiye. Yeh fast aur cheap hai, lekin biased ho sakta hai, kyunki har example ke select hone ki probability barabar nahi hoti.

Simple random sampling

Har example ke select hone ki probability barabar hoti hai. Yeh unbiased hai aur implement karna aasan hai, lekin rare classes ke examples miss ho sakte hain — agar ek class sirf 1% data me hai, to random sample me woh aur bhi kam dikh sakti hai.

Stratified sampling

Data ko pehle groups (strata) me baanto — jaise class ya age group ke hisaab se — phir har group se proportionally sample lo. Isse har group ki representation bani rehti hai. Imbalanced data ke liye yeh random sampling se behtar hai.

Weighted sampling

Har example ko ek weight diya jata hai, aur weight ke proportion me select hone ki probability milti hai. Sample weights decision boundary ko significantly badal sakte hain — ek class ko zyada weight dene se model us class par zyada dhyaan deta hai.

Importance sampling

Jab tum jis distribution se sample kar rahe ho woh target distribution se alag ho, to importance sampling weights ko adjust karke bias ko correct karta hai. Isme proposal distribution Q(x) se sample karke target distribution P(x) ke hisaab se weights lagaye jate hain.

Sampling ka choice model ki performance aur fairness dono ko affect karta hai. Galat sampling se model ko lagta hai ki duniya waisi hai jaisi sample me dikhi — jabki asal duniya alag ho sakti hai.

Weighted sampling with random.choices — Python · book se verbatim
pythonbook se, jaisa chhapa hai
# Choose two items from the list such that 1, 2, 3, 4 each has
# 20% chance of being selected, while 100 and 1000 each have only 10% chance.
random.choices(population=[1, 2, 3, 4, 100, 1000],
                     weights=[0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.1, 0.1],
               k=2)
# This is equivalent to the following
random.choices(population=[1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 100, 1000],
               k=2)
Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaBatch processing vs stream processingAgla →Reservoir sampling — streaming data se sample
03.2Chapter 3 — Training Data

Reservoir sampling — streaming data se sample

Jab data stream ki tarah aa raha ho aur tumhe pata hi na ho ki total kitna data aayega, to random sampling kaise karein? Reservoir sampling iska jawab hai.

Kaise kaam karta hai

Tum ek fixed-size reservoir (jaise k=1000 slots) rakhte ho. Pehle k items ko seedha reservoir me daal do. Phir har naya item (n-th item, jahan n > k) ko k/n probability ke saath reservoir me lo, aur agar lo to reservoir ke ek random item ko replace kar do.

Isse stream ke end me reservoir me har item ke hone ki probability barabar hoti hai — chahe stream kitna bhi lamba ho. Memory bhi fixed rehti hai, kyunki poora stream store nahi karna padta.

Kab use karein

  • Logs ya events ki endless stream se representative sample chahiye ho.
  • Data itna bada ho ki use memory me rakhna possible na ho.
  • Online learning ke liye recent data ka unbiased sample chahiye ho.

Reservoir sampling ka ek limitation yeh hai ki yeh uniform sampling karta hai — agar tumhe recent data ko zyada weight dena hai, to iska weighted version chahiye hoga.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaSampling — sahi data chunnaAgla →Labeling aur label multiplicity
03.3Chapter 3 — Training Data

Labeling aur label multiplicity

Supervised ML ko labels chahiye hote hain, aur labels banana mehenga, slow aur mushkil kaam hai. Labels ki quality seedha model ki quality tay karti hai.

Hand labels

Human annotators se labels banwana sabse reliable tareeka hai, lekin mehenga aur slow hai. Annotators ko clear guidelines chahiye hoti hain, aur phir bhi unme disagreement ho sakta hai.

Label multiplicity — ek hi example, kai labels

Ek hi example ke liye alag annotators alag labels de sakte hain. Example: teen annotators ko ek hi text diya gaya, aur teeno ne alag label diya. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki koi ek galat hai — task hi ambiguous ho sakta hai, ya guidelines unclear ho sakti hain.

Label multiplicity ko handle karne ke tareeke:

  • Majority vote: jo label sabse zyada annotators ne diya, woh lo. Simple hai, lekin minority opinion kho jati hai.
  • Average ya soft labels: labels ko probabilities ke roop me rakho, taaki uncertainty bani rahe.
  • Guidelines sudharo: agar disagreement zyada hai, to pehle annotation guidelines aur examples ko clear karo.

Ek important lesson: labels "ground truth" nahi hote — woh human judgment hote hain, aur unme bhi bias aur galtiyan ho sakti hain. Isliye labeling process ko bhi monitor aur improve karna chahiye, jaise model ko karte ho.

Labeling function (weak supervision heuristic) — Python · book se verbatim
pythonbook se, jaisa chhapa hai
def labeling_function(note):
   if "pneumonia" in note:
         return "EMERGENT"

Note: is code ki indentation bhi bilkul waisi hi hai jaisi book me chhapi hai (3 spaces, phir 9 spaces) — jaisa chhapa hai waisa hi dikhaya gaya hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaReservoir sampling — streaming data se sampleAgla →Data lineage — data kahan se aaya, kahan gaya
03.4Chapter 3 — Training Data

Data lineage — data kahan se aaya, kahan gaya

Data lineage ka matlab hai: har dataset ka poora history track karna — woh kahan se aaya, kisne use transform kiya, kaunsi pipeline se guzra, aur kaunse model ne use use kiya.

Kyun zaroori hai

  • Debugging: model galat predictions de raha hai to pata lagao — kya training data me kuch badla? Kaunsi pipeline version use hui thi?
  • Reproducibility: purana experiment dobara chalana ho to wahi data, wahi code, wahi config chahiye. Bina lineage ke yeh guesswork ban jata hai.
  • Compliance: privacy regulations me poochha ja sakta hai ki ek user ka data kahan-kahan use hua. Lineage ke bina jawab dena mushkil hai.
  • Data quality: agar upstream source me galti aayi, to lineage se pata chalta hai ki kaunse downstream datasets aur models affect hue.

Kya track karein

Source systems, transformations, versions, timestamps, aur kaunse models ne kaunsa data use kiya — yeh sab lineage ka hissa hai. Modern data platforms me lineage automatic capture hoti hai, lekin chhoti teams ko ise manually ya simple tooling se karna padta hai.

Data lineage ko "data ka family tree" samjho — bina iske tumhe pata nahi chalega ki tumhara model kis par khada hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaLabeling aur label multiplicityAgla →Jab hand labels na hon — weak supervision, semi-supervision, transfer learning
03.5Chapter 3 — Training Data

Jab hand labels na hon — weak supervision, semi-supervision, transfer learning

Har problem me hazaaron hand labels banana possible nahi hota. Book 3 tareeke batati hai jinse kam labels me bhi kaam chalaya ja sakta hai.

Weak supervision

Isme hand labels ki jagah labeling functions use hote hain — chhote heuristic programs jo data ko automatically label karte hain. Example: agar text me "http" hai to use spam mano. Ek labeling function noisy ho sakta hai, lekin kai functions ko combine karke — unke agreements aur disagreements se — probabilistic labels banaye jate hain. Hand labeling ke mukable weak supervision ke fayde: fast hai, cheap hai, aur domain knowledge ko code me daala ja sakta hai. Lekin labels noisy hote hain, aur labeling functions likhna bhi ek skill hai.

Semi-supervision

Isme thode se labeled examples aur bahut saare unlabeled examples ko saath use kiya jata hai. Model pehle labeled data par train hota hai, phir unlabeled data par apni confident predictions ko pseudo-labels ki tarah use karke aur seekhta hai. Yeh tab kaam karta hai jab labeled aur unlabeled data ka distribution similar ho.

Transfer learning

Ek bade dataset par train hue model ko apne chhote dataset par fine-tune karo. Example: ek bada language model jo bahut saare text par train hua hai, use apne specific task ke liye adapt karna. Few-shot learning me to model ko sirf kuch examples se hi naya task sikha diya jata hai. Transfer learning ne labeling ki zaroorat ko bahut kam kar diya hai, lekin yeh tabhi kaam karta hai jab source aur target tasks related hon.

Teeno tareekon me ek common baat hai: labels ki kami ko data aur prior knowledge se compensate karo, blindly aur labels ka wait mat karo.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaData lineage — data kahan se aaya, kahan gayaAgla →Active learning — model khud bataye kya label karein
03.6Chapter 3 — Training Data

Active learning — model khud bataye kya label karein

Active learning me model khud batata hai ki kaunse examples label karne se use sabse zyada fayda hoga. Randomly examples label karne ki jagah, sirf wahi examples label karo jo model ke liye sabse informative hon.

Uncertainty-based active learning

Sabse common approach: woh examples chuno jin par model sabse zyada uncertain hai — jaise jahan do classes ki probabilities lagbhag barabar hon. Ek toy example me 400 instances the, jo do groups se evenly sample hue the. Model ne pehle kuch examples par train karke decision boundary banayi, phir boundary ke paas wale uncertain examples ko label karne ke liye chuna — aur har round me boundary behtar hoti gayi.

Kab useful hai

  • Labeling mehenga ho — jaise medical images jahan expert chahiye.
  • Unlabeled data bahut zyada ho, lekin label karne ka budget kam ho.
  • Model ko rare ya borderline cases seekhne hon.

Dhyan rakhne wali baatein

Active learning se training data ka distribution badal jata hai — model uncertain examples par zyada focus karta hai, isliye training distribution real-world distribution se alag ho jata hai. Yeh covariate shift ka ek cause hai, jo aage Chapter 7 me discuss hoga. Isliye active learning ke fayde ke saath is side effect ko bhi samajhna chahiye.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaJab hand labels na hon — weak supervision, semi-supervision, transfer learningAgla →Class imbalance — jab ek class bahut kam ho
03.7Chapter 3 — Training Data

Class imbalance — jab ek class bahut kam ho

Real-world data aksar imbalanced hota hai — jaise fraud transactions 1% se bhi kam hote hain, ya ek rare disease ke cases bahut kam hote hain. ML aise data par mushkil se seekhta hai, kyunki model majority class predict karke bhi high accuracy dikha sakta hai.

Challenges

Imbalanced classes me accuracy misleading hoti hai: 99% accuracy ka matlab ho sakta hai ki model ne minority class ko kabhi predict hi nahi kiya. Isliye sahi evaluation metrics chahiye — precision, recall, F1 score, aur PR curve (precision-recall curve). ROC curve bhi use hota hai, lekin highly imbalanced data me PR curve zyada informative hoti hai.

Data-level methods — resampling

  • Undersampling: majority class ke examples kam kar do. Fast hai, lekin data waste hota hai.
  • Oversampling: minority class ke examples duplicate karke badha do. Data waste nahi hota, lekin overfitting ka risk badhta hai.

Algorithm-level methods

  • Cost-sensitive learning: galat predictions ki cost class ke hisaab se alag rakho — minority class ko galat predict karna zyada mehenga mano. Loss function me cost matrix Cij use hoti hai.
  • Class-balanced loss: har class ko uski frequency ke inverse proportion me weight do, taaki rare classes ka loss zyada matter kare.
  • Focal loss: easy examples ka loss kam kar do, taaki model hard examples par focus kare. Focal loss se trained model ka loss cross-entropy se trained model se kam dikha experiments me.

Yaad rakho: resampling ya loss change karne se training distribution badalta hai — iska asar deployment par bhi padta hai, isliye evaluation hamesha original distribution par karo.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaActive learning — model khud bataye kya label kareinAgla →Data augmentation aur synthesis
03.8Chapter 3 — Training Data

Data augmentation aur synthesis

Jab data kam ho ya model overfit kar raha ho, to existing data se naya data banana — augmentation — ek powerful tareeka hai.

Simple label-preserving transformations

Transformations jo label ko badle bina data ko badal dein. Images ke liye: crop, flip, rotate, color change. Text ke liye: synonym replace, word drop, back-translation. Audio ke liye: speed ya pitch change. Key rule: transformation ke baad label wahi rehna chahiye — agar image flip karne se label badal jaye, to woh transformation galat hai.

Perturbation

Data me chhoti si noise daal kar model ko robust banao. Lekin dhyaan rakho: neural networks bahut sensitive ho sakte hain — ek pixel badalne se bhi model galat predict kar sakta hai. Isliye perturbation ko carefully test karo.

Data synthesis

Jab real data milna mushkil ho, to synthetic data generate karo — simulations se, ya generative models se. Synthetic data privacy issues ko bhi kam kar sakta hai, kyunki real users ka data use nahi hota. Lekin synthetic data real data ki jagah poori tarah nahi le sakta — agar synthetic data ka distribution real se alag hua, to model real duniya me fail karega.

Augmentation ek free lunch nahi hai: galat augmentation se model galat patterns seekh sakta hai. Har augmentation ko validation data par test karo.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaClass imbalance — jab ek class bahut kam hoAgla →Learned features vs engineered features
04.1Chapter 4 — Feature Engineering

Learned features vs engineered features

Features woh inputs hote hain jo model ko diye jate hain. Do tareeke hain features banane ke: handcraft karo (engineered) ya model ko seekhne do (learned).

Engineered features

Domain knowledge se manually banaye gaye features. Example: text ke liye n-gram features — ek post ko 7 n-grams ki vocabulary se vector banana. Ya ek comment ke baare me features: comment ki length, thread ka size, user ka history. Engineered features interpretable hote hain aur kam data me bhi kaam karte hain.

Learned features

Deep learning models apne aap features seekhte hain — pehli layers simple patterns, baad ki layers complex patterns. Yeh tab best hote hain jab bahut saara data ho aur domain knowledge kam ho. Lekin learned features ko samajhna mushkil hota hai, aur unhe train karne me zyada data aur compute chahiye.

Kaunsa kab

  • Engineered: jab data kam ho, domain knowledge strong ho, ya interpretability chahiye ho.
  • Learned: jab data bahut zyada ho aur raw inputs (images, text, audio) se patterns nikalne hon.
  • Dono ka mix: aksar best results dono ko combine karne se aate hain — learned features ke saath kuch engineered features bhi do.

Ek aur baat: features sirf model ki accuracy nahi, poori system ki cost bhi tay karte hain. Har feature ko compute, store aur maintain karna padta hai — isliye bekaar features technical debt ban jate hain.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaData augmentation aur synthesisAgla →Missing values — khaali jagah ka kya karein
04.2Chapter 4 — Feature Engineering

Missing values — khaali jagah ka kya karein

Real data me missing values common hain. Inhe handle karna ek aisi skill hai jo interviews me bhi poochhi jati hai — aur jise kai ML engineers theek se nahi jante.

Missing values ke types

  • MCAR (Missing Completely At Random): missing hona kisi bhi observed ya unobserved value par depend nahi karta — pure random hai.
  • MAR (Missing At Random): missing hona observed values par depend karta hai, lekin missing value khud par nahi.
  • MNAR (Missing Not At Random): missing hona missing value khud par depend karta hai. Example: zyada income wale log apni income batana nahi chahte — isliye income missing hai, aur woh missing hona income ki value se juda hai.

Type jaanna isliye zaroori hai kyunki har type ka sahi treatment alag hota hai. MNAR ko ignore karna sabse dangerous hai, kyunki wahan missing hona hi ek signal hai.

Deletion

Missing values wale examples ya columns ko delete kar do. Simple hai, lekin data waste hota hai aur bias aa sakta hai — agar missing values randomly nahi hain, to delete karne se distribution badal jayegi.

Imputation

Missing values ko kisi value se bhar do — mean, median, mode, ya model se predict karke. Imputation data bachata hai, lekin galat imputation model ko galat signal de sakta hai. Ek achha tareeka hai missing hone ko khud ek feature banana — jaise "age_missing" naam ka binary feature — taaki model ko pata chale ki value missing thi.

Interviews me aksar log deletion prefer karte hain, lekin experienced engineers imputation aur missingness ko feature banane ki baat karte hain. Missing values ko handle karne ka tareeka model ki performance se seedha juda hota hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaLearned features vs engineered featuresAgla →Scaling — features ko ek scale par laana
04.3Chapter 4 — Feature Engineering

Scaling — features ko ek scale par laana

Alag features ke alag scales hote hain — ek feature 0 se 1 ke beech, doosra 0 se 1,00,000 tak. Bina scaling ke model bade scale wale feature ko zyada important samajh sakta hai.

Common scaling methods

  • Standardization (z-score): har value se mean ghatao aur standard deviation se divide karo. Result me mean 0 aur standard deviation 1 hota hai. Outliers ke liye relatively robust hai.
  • Normalization (min-max): values ko 0 se 1 ke beech le aao. Simple hai, lekin outliers se bahut affect hota hai — ek bada outlier baaki saari values ko chhota bana deta hai.
  • Log transformation: skewed data ke liye. Log transform se data ka skew kam hota hai aur distribution normal ke kareeb aati hai. Income jaise data par yeh bahut kaam karta hai.

Scaling kab zaroori hai

Distance-based models (jaise k-NN) aur gradient-based models (jaise neural networks) ko scaling ki zyada zaroorat hoti hai. Tree-based models ko scaling se zyada farq nahi padta, kyunki woh thresholds par split karte hain.

Ek critical rule: scaling ke parameters (mean, std, min, max) sirf training data se compute karo, aur wahi parameters test aur production data par apply karo. Agar scaling se pehle data split nahi kiya, to leakage ho jayega — yeh aage 04.6 me detail me hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaMissing values — khaali jagah ka kya kareinAgla →Discretization aur categorical encoding
04.4Chapter 4 — Feature Engineering

Discretization aur categorical encoding

Continuous values ko groups me baantna (discretization) aur categorical values ko numbers me badalna (encoding) — dono feature engineering ke basic operations hain.

Discretization

Continuous feature ko bins me baanto. Example: income ko "lower (35,000 se kam)", "middle (35,000–1,00,000)" aur "upper (1,00,000 se zyada)" me baantna; age ko "18 se kam, 18–22, 22–30, 30–40, 40–65, 65 se zyada" me baantna. Isse model ko non-linear patterns seekhna aasan ho jata hai aur outliers ka asar kam hota hai. Lekin bins ke boundaries choose karna ek decision hai — galat boundaries information kho sakti hain.

Encoding categorical features

  • One-hot encoding: har category ke liye ek binary column banao. Simple aur interpretable hai, lekin categories zyada hon to columns bahut badh jate hain.
  • Feature hashing: categories ko hash function se fixed number of columns me map karo. Columns kam hote hain, lekin collisions hote hain — do alag categories ek hi column me aa sakti hain. Experiments me 50% collision rate par bhi log loss me aadha percent se kam ka nuksaan dikha, isliye hashing practical hai.
  • Embeddings: categories ko dense vectors me badlo jo training ke dauraan seekhe jate hain. Similar categories ke vectors paas aate hain. Yeh high-cardinality categorical features ke liye best hai.

Encoding choose karte time cardinality dekho: kam categories hon to one-hot, zyada hon to hashing ya embeddings.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaScaling — features ko ek scale par laanaAgla →Feature crossing aur positional embeddings
04.5Chapter 4 — Feature Engineering

Feature crossing aur positional embeddings

Akela feature kabhi-kabhi kaafi nahi hota — do features ka combination zyada informative ho sakta hai. Isi ko feature crossing kehte hain.

Feature crossing

Do ya zyada features ko combine karke naya feature banao. Example: location aur time ka combination — ek jagah din me safe ho sakti hai lekin raat me nahi. Crossing se model ko aise interactions seekhne me madad milti hai jo single features se nahi milti. Lekin crossings ki sankhya bahut fast badhti hai, isliye sirf meaningful crossings banao, har combination nahi.

Positional embeddings

Sequence models (jaise transformers) ko yeh jaanna chahiye ki ek element sequence me kis position par hai. Iske liye positional embeddings use hote hain.

  • Discrete positional embeddings: har position ke liye ek learned vector rakho.
  • Continuous positional embeddings: position ko sine aur cosine functions se encode karo — even index par sine, odd index par cosine. Isse model ko relative positions ka bhi pata chalta hai, aur yeh unseen lengths par bhi kaam karta hai.

Ek naive example: gaane ki recommendation me "kya gaana pehle position par dikhaya gaya tha" ek feature ho sakta hai — lekin yeh feature training aur inference me alag behave karta hai, jo leakage aur feedback loops ka cause banta hai (Chapter 7 me detail me).

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaDiscretization aur categorical encodingAgla →Data leakage — sabse khatarnaak galti
04.6Chapter 4 — Feature Engineering

Data leakage — sabse khatarnaak galti

Data leakage tab hota hai jab training data me aisi information aa jaye jo inference ke time available nahi hogi. Model training me bahut achha dikhega, lekin production me fail hoga. Yeh ML ki sabse common aur khatarnaak galtiyon me se ek hai.

Leakage ke 6 common causes

  1. Time-correlated data ko randomly split karna: time se juda data (jaise week 5 ka data) ko randomly train/validation/test me baantne se future ki information training me leak ho jati hai. Solution: time ke hisaab se split karo.
  2. Split se pehle scaling karna: poore data par mean/std compute karke phir split karne se test data ki information training me aa jati hai.
  3. Split se pehle oversampling ya augmentation karna: duplicate examples train aur test dono me aa sakte hain.
  4. Duplication ko split se pehle handle na karna: same user ya same item ke examples train aur test dono me hon to model memorize kar leta hai.
  5. Group leakage: ek hi group (jaise ek hi user ya ek hi patient) ke examples train aur test dono me hon.
  6. Data collection process se leakage: data collect karte time hi label ki information features me aa jana.

Ek mashhoor kahani

Ek bade competition me leakage ki wajah se ek team ka model leaderboard par bahut achha dikha, lekin woh information use kar raha tha jo real predictions ke time available nahi hoti. Yeh yaad dilata hai ki high validation score hamesha achhe model ka proof nahi hota.

Leakage kaise detect karein

  • Validation score suspiciously high ho to shak karo.
  • Feature importance check karo — agar ek feature bahut zyada important dikh raha hai, to ho sakta hai woh leaked ho.
  • Ablation karo: suspicious feature ko hata kar dekho ki performance kitni girti hai.
  • Train aur test ka distribution compare karo.
Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaFeature crossing aur positional embeddingsAgla →Achhe features kaise banayein — importance aur generalization
04.7Chapter 4 — Feature Engineering

Achhe features kaise banayein — importance aur generalization

Features banane ke baad sawal yeh hai: kaunse features achhe hain aur kaunse bekaar? Iske liye feature importance aur generalization ko samajhna zaroori hai.

Feature importance

Feature importance batata hai ki har feature model ki predictions me kitna contribute karta hai. SHAP jaise methods se pata chalta hai ki ek single prediction me har feature ka kitna contribution tha, aur poore model me kaunsa feature sabse important hai. Ek example me ek housing feature ka ek value sabse zyada contribute kar raha tha, aur overall bhi wahi feature sabse important tha.

Lekin importance ko blindly trust mat karo: correlated features me importance baant jata hai, aur ek feature important isliye bhi dikh sakta hai kyunki woh leaked hai.

Feature generalization

Achha feature woh hai jo training data ke bahar bhi kaam kare — naye users, naye time periods, naye regions par. Agar ek feature sirf training data me achha hai lekin production me nahi, to woh overfitting ka cause hai. Features ko alag time periods aur alag user groups par test karo.

Bekaar features technical debt hain

Har feature ki cost hoti hai: use compute karna, store karna, monitor karna, aur jab pipeline badle to use update karna. Agar ek feature model ki performance me 1% se kam contribute karta hai — jaise ek study me kai features ka contribution 1% se kam tha — to use hata dena behtar ho sakta hai. Kam, achhe features zyada, bekaar features se behtar hote hain.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaData leakage — sabse khatarnaak galtiAgla →ML problems ko frame karna — task types
05.1Chapter 5 — Model Development

ML problems ko frame karna — task types

Model banane se pehle problem ko sahi tareeke se frame karna zaroori hai. Galat framing se best algorithm bhi bekaar ho jata hai.

Common task types

  • Classification: output ek category ho — jaise spam ya not spam, ya kaunsi bimari hai.
  • Regression: output ek continuous value ho — jaise ghar ki keemat ya demand ka number.

Classification ke subtypes

  • Binary classification: sirf do classes — jaise fraud ya genuine.
  • Multiclass classification: 2 se zyada classes, lekin har example sirf ek class me aata hai — jaise ek image me kaunsa animal hai.
  • Multilabel classification: ek example par kai labels lag sakte hain — jaise ek article par "sports" aur "politics" dono tags hon.

Ek hi problem, kai framings

Ek hi business problem ko kai tareekon se frame kiya ja sakta hai. Example: user agla kaunsa app kholega, yeh predict karna. Ise classification ki tarah frame kar sakte ho (kaunsa app), ranking ki tarah (apps ko order karo), ya regression ki tarah (har app ke khulne ki probability). Har framing se alag model, alag metrics aur alag tradeoffs aate hain. Sahi framing woh hai jo business goal se sabse kareeb ho aur jiske liye data available ho.

Framing karte time yeh bhi socho: output kya hoga, labels kahan se aayenge, aur model ki galti ki cost kya hogi. Framing galat ho to baad me poora system dobara banana padta hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 5
← PichhlaAchhe features kaise banayein — importance aur generalizationAgla →Objective functions aur decoupling objectives
05.2Chapter 5 — Model Development

Objective functions aur decoupling objectives

Objective function woh hai jise model optimize karta hai. Lekin business goal aur objective function aksar ek hi cheez nahi hote — aur yahi gap kai failures ka cause hai.

Decoupling objectives

Ek social media feed ka example lo. Business chahta hai ki users ko quality content mile. Lekin "quality" ko seedha optimize nahi kar sakte. Isliye objectives ko decouple karo:

  1. Spam filter karo.
  2. NSFW content filter karo.
  3. Misinformation filter karo.
  4. Bache hue posts ko quality ke hisaab se rank karo.

Har step ka apna model ya rule ho sakta hai. Isse har objective ko alag se measure aur improve kar sakte ho. Agar sab kuch ek hi model me daal doge, to pata nahi chalega ki kaunsa hissa fail ho raha hai.

Quality loss

Ranking ke liye quality loss define karo — model ki ranking aur ideal ranking ke beech ka difference. Do models ho sakte hain: ek jo harmful content ko filter kare, aur ek jo quality ke hisaab se rank kare. Dono ke objectives alag hain, isliye dono ko alag se evaluate karo.

Yaad rakho: model wahi optimize karega jo tumne loss function me likha hai — jo tum chahte ho woh nahi. Isliye objective function ko business goal se carefully align karo.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 5
← PichhlaML problems ko frame karna — task typesAgla →Model selection — 6 tips
05.3Chapter 5 — Model Development

Model selection — 6 tips

Model choose karna sirf accuracy dekh kar nahi hota. Book 6 tips deti hai jo model selection me kaam aati hain.

6 tips

  1. State-of-the-art trap se bacho: latest research model hamesha best nahi hota. Research models academic settings me evaluate hote hain, jahan data clean aur compute unlimited hota hai. Production me unki cost aur complexity bahut zyada ho sakti hai.
  2. Sabse simple model se shuru karo: simple model baseline deta hai, fast iterate hota hai, aur usse pata chalta hai ki ML se kitna fayda ho raha hai. Kai baar simple model hi kaafi hota hai.
  3. Human biases se bacho: log apne favourite models ko prefer karte hain, ya jo model unhe familiar hai use choose karte hain. Model ko data aur metrics se choose karo, preference se nahi.
  4. Abhi achha vs baad me achha: ek model abhi achha ho sakta hai lekin jab data badhe to doosra model behtar ho jaye. Learning curves dekho — jaise ek simple model kam data par behtar ho, lekin zyada data par ek complex model aage nikal jaye.
  5. Trade-offs evaluate karo: accuracy ke saath latency, compute cost, interpretability aur maintainability bhi dekho. Ek model thoda kam accurate lekin 10x fast ho, to production me woh behtar ho sakta hai.
  6. Model ke assumptions samjho: har model kuch assume karta hai — jaise data independent aur identically distributed (IID) hai, ya decision boundaries smooth hain, ya features conditionally independent hain, ya data normally distributed hai. Agar tumhara data in assumptions ko violate karta hai, to model fail karega.

Model selection ek baar ka kaam nahi hai — data aur requirements badalte rehte hain, isliye models ko dobara evaluate karte rehna chahiye.

Cross entropy in Python — Python · book se verbatim
pythonbook se, jaisa chhapa hai
import numpy as np
def cross_entropy(p, q):
return -sum([p[i] * np.log(q[i]) for i in range(len(p))])
p = [0, 0, 0, 1]
q = [0.45, 0.2, 0.02, 0.33]
cross_entropy(p, q)

Note: upar wala code bilkul waisa hi hai jaisa book me chhapa hai — return -sum(...) wali line ki indentation book me bhi aisi hi hai (bina indent ke), isliye yeh jaisa chhapa hai waisa hi dikhaya gaya hai, theek nahi kiya gaya.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 5
← PichhlaObjective functions aur decoupling objectivesAgla →Ensembles — bagging, boosting, stacking
05.4Chapter 5 — Model Development

Ensembles — bagging, boosting, stacking

Ensemble ka matlab hai kai models ko combine karke ek behtar model banana. Aaj ke top solutions — chahe woh ek image classification competition ho ya ek question-answering benchmark — aksar ensembles hote hain.

Bagging

Bagging (bootstrap aggregating) me data ke alag-alag random samples par kai models train kiye jate hain, aur unki predictions ko average ya vote karke combine kiya jata hai. Isse variance kam hoti hai. Bagging unstable methods — jaise neural networks aur decision trees — par khaas taur par achha kaam karta hai. Random forests bagging ka hi ek famous example hai.

Boosting

Boosting me models sequentially train hote hain — har naya model pichhle models ki galtiyon par focus karta hai. Weak learners ko combine karke strong learner banaya jata hai. Boosting bias kam karta hai, lekin overfitting ka risk zyada hota hai aur training slow hoti hai.

Stacking

Stacking me kai base learners ki predictions ko ek meta-learner ko input ki tarah diya jata hai, jo final prediction banata hai. Meta-learner simple bhi ho sakta hai — jaise logistic regression. Stacking tab best kaam karta hai jab base learners diverse hon — alag algorithms, alag features, alag data.

Ensembles accuracy badhate hain, lekin cost bhi badhate hain: zyada models train karne, deploy karne aur maintain karne padte hain. Isliye production me hamesha socho ki ensemble ka fayda uski cost se zyada hai ya nahi.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 5
← PichhlaModel selection — 6 tipsAgla →Experiment tracking, versioning aur debugging
05.5Chapter 5 — Model Development

Experiment tracking, versioning aur debugging

ML development me experiments ki sankhya bahut fast badhti hai. Bina tracking ke tumhe yaad nahi rahega ki kaunsa model kis data aur kis config par train hua tha.

Experiment tracking

Har experiment ke liye track karo: data version, code version, hyperparameters, metrics, aur system performance metrics jaise memory usage aur CPU/GPU utilization. System metrics bottlenecks pehchanne me madad karte hain. Tracking ke bina do experiments ko compare karna impossible ho jata hai.

Versioning

Code ke saath data aur models ko bhi version karo. Ek model ko reproduce karne ke liye teeno chahiye: wahi code, wahi data, wahi config. Agar koi ek missing hai, to results dobara nahi milenge.

Debugging ML models — 3 practical tips

  1. Simple se shuru karo, dheere-dheere components add karo: seedha bada open-source model clone karke shuru mat karo. Pehle chhota model chalao, phir complexity badhao — taaki jab kuch toote to pata chale ki kaunsa component toota.
  2. Ek hi batch par overfit karo: model ko ek chhote se batch par train karke dekho ki woh use memorize kar pata hai ya nahi. Agar ek batch par bhi overfit nahi kar pata, to model ya training pipeline me bug hai.
  3. Random seed set karo: randomness ki wajah se results har run me alag ho sakte hain. Seed set karne se runs comparable hote hain aur debugging aasan hoti hai.

Debugging ke time yeh bhi check karo: theoretical constraints (kya model ke assumptions violate ho rahe hain), features ka choice, aur data ki quality. Aksar bug model me nahi, data me hota hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 5
← PichhlaEnsembles — bagging, boosting, stackingAgla →Distributed training, AutoML aur development ke 4 phases
05.6Chapter 5 — Model Development

Distributed training, AutoML aur development ke 4 phases

Jab models aur datasets bade ho jate hain, to ek machine kaafi nahi hoti. Distributed training aur AutoML is problem ko solve karte hain.

Distributed training

  • Data parallelism: data ko alag machines par baanto, har machine par model ka poora copy train karo, aur gradients ko sync karo. Synchronous SGD (SSGD) me sab machines ek saath sync hoti hain; asynchronous SGD (ASGD) me har machine apni speed par update karti hai.
  • Model parallelism: model ko hi alag machines par baanto — jaise ek machine pehli layers, doosri machine agli layers. Yeh tab zaroori hota hai jab model ek machine ki memory me fit hi na ho.
  • Pipeline parallelism: model parallelism ka ek smarter version — alag micro-batches ko pipeline ki tarah process karo, taaki koi machine idle na rahe.
  • Data aur model parallelism ek saath bhi use kiye ja sakte hain.

AutoML

  • Soft AutoML — hyperparameter tuning: random search, grid search aur smarter methods se best hyperparameters dhoondhna. Aksar weak models bhi well-tuned hyperparameters ke saath strong models ko hara dete hain.
  • Hard AutoML — architecture search aur learned optimizer: model ki architecture khud search karna, ya optimizer ko bhi seekhna. Yeh bahut compute khata hai aur sirf bade players ke liye practical hai.

ML model development ke 4 phases

  1. Phase 1 — ML se pehle: bina ML ke system chalao. Ek bade social network ka feed 2006 me bina ML ke launch hua tha — pehle heuristics se kaam chalao, taaki pata chale ki ML ki zaroorat hai bhi ya nahi.
  2. Phase 2 — simplest ML models: simple models se shuru karo aur infrastructure banao.
  3. Phase 3 — simple models ko optimize karo: features, tuning aur evaluation par focus karo.
  4. Phase 4 — complex systems: jab simple models ki limit aa jaye, tab complex systems banao.

Har phase ko skip karke seedha Phase 4 par jaana aksar barbaadi hoti hai — infrastructure aur understanding dono missing hote hain.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 5
← PichhlaExperiment tracking, versioning aur debuggingAgla →Offline evaluation — baselines, tests, calibration aur slices
05.7Chapter 5 — Model Development

Offline evaluation — baselines, tests, calibration aur slices

Evaluation metrics akele kuch nahi kehte — unka matlab baselines ke comparison me hota hai. Offline evaluation ka matlab hai model ko deploy karne se pehle test data par check karna.

Baselines — 5 types

  • Random baseline: random predictions se kitna behtar ho?
  • Simple heuristic: simple rules se kitna behtar ho?
  • Zero rule baseline: hamesha majority class predict karne se kitna behtar ho?
  • Human baseline: insaan kitna achha karta hai? Kai tasks me human performance hi target hoti hai.
  • Existing solutions: jo system abhi production me hai, usse kitna behtar ho?

Behavioural tests — 3 types

  • Perturbation tests: input me chhota change karo — prediction stable rehni chahiye. Agar ek word badalne se prediction poori badal jaye, to model fragile hai.
  • Invariance tests: input me aisa change jo prediction ko badalna nahi chahiye — jaise naam badalne se sentiment nahi badalna chahiye.
  • Directional expectation tests: input me aisa change jo prediction ko ek expected direction me badle — jaise price badhne se demand kam honi chahiye.

Calibration aur confidence

Calibration ka matlab hai ki model ki confidence uski accuracy se match kare. Agar model 90% confident hai to use 90% baar sahi hona chahiye. Calibration curves se pata chalta hai ki kaunsa model overconfident ya underconfident hai. Confidence measurement system-level hota hai — poore system ki reliability ke liye zaroori hai.

Slice-based evaluation aur fairness

Overall accuracy achhi hone se matlab nahi — har slice par check karo: alag user groups, alag regions, alag time periods. Slices banane ke tareeke: heuristics se, ya error analysis se — misclassified examples ko manually dekh kar patterns dhoondhna. Ek mashhoor example: ek bade university me overall admission rate se lagta tha ki ek group ke saath bias hai, lekin department-wise dekhne par picture ulta nikla — yahi aggregation paradox hai: aggregate dekhne par result ulta dikh sakta hai. Isliye aggregate metrics par bharosa mat karo, slices par dekho.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 5
← PichhlaDistributed training, AutoML aur development ke 4 phasesAgla →Deployment myths — scale ka matlab kya hai
06.1Chapter 6 — Model Deployment

Deployment myths — scale ka matlab kya hai

Deployment ke baare me kai myths hain. Book unhe todti hai aur batati hai ki "scale" ka matlab har application ke liye alag hota hai.

Common myths

  • Myth: deployment ek baar ka kaam hai. Asliyat: deployment ke baad monitoring aur updates chalte rehte hain. Model deploy karna end nahi, shuruaat hai.
  • Myth: zyada scale ka matlab hai zyada users. Scale kai tareekon se badhta hai — traffic, data volume, model count. Ek chhoti company ke 100 employees bhi alag scale ka challenge hain.
  • Myth: ML engineers ko scale ki chinta nahi karni chahiye. Asliyat: scale ke decisions — batch ya online, cloud ya edge — model design ko shuru se affect karte hain.

Model logic ke parts

Prediction banane ke liye sirf model nahi chahiye — model logic me kai cheezein aati hain: raw data se features banana, model ko run karna, aur predictions ko post-process karna. Deployment ka matlab hai is poori logic ko production me chalana, sirf model file ko nahi.

Ek aur baat: ek company me alag-alag tasks ke liye kai models hote hain — ek badi streaming company ke example me kai tasks par ML use hota hai. Isliye deployment ko ek model ke hisaab se nahi, poori system ke hisaab se sochna chahiye.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 6
← PichhlaOffline evaluation — baselines, tests, calibration aur slicesAgla →Batch prediction vs online prediction
06.2Chapter 6 — Model Deployment

Batch prediction vs online prediction

Predictions generate karne ke do main tareeke hain: batch aur online. Dono ki architecture, cost aur use cases alag hain.

Batch prediction

Predictions periodically generate ki jati hain — jaise roz ek baar, ya har ghante. Features bhi batch me compute hote hain. Yeh asynchronous hota hai: user ko turant jawab nahi chahiye hota. Example: food delivery apps restaurant recommendations ko batch me generate karte hain. Batch prediction cheap aur simple hota hai, aur bade volumes ke liye efficient hai.

Online prediction

Predictions request aate hi, real-time me generate ki jati hain — synchronous. User wait kar raha hota hai, isliye latency critical hoti hai. Online prediction me do types hain:

  • Sirf batch features ke saath: features pehle se compute karke store kiye hote hain, inference ke time sirf lookup hota hai. Simple hai, lekin features stale ho sakte hain.
  • Batch + streaming features ke saath: historical batch features ke saath real-time streaming features bhi use hote hain. Zyada fresh aur accurate, lekin architecture complex hoti hai.

Key differences — ek table ke hisaab se

  • Batch: asynchronous, periodic, high throughput, latency kam important, cost kam.
  • Online: synchronous, real-time, latency critical, cost zyada, infrastructure complex.

Choice business requirement se aati hai: agar user ko turant result chahiye, to online; agar result pehle se compute karke rakha ja sakta hai, to batch kaafi hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 6
← PichhlaDeployment myths — scale ka matlab kya haiAgla →Batch se online tak — aur train/serve skew
06.3Chapter 6 — Model Deployment

Batch se online tak — aur train/serve skew

Kai systems batch prediction se shuru hokar online prediction ki taraf badhte hain. Yeh transition architecture ko poori tarah badal deta hai — aur isme sabse bada khatra train/serve skew hai.

Transition kaise hoti hai

Pehle batch pipeline se predictions bante hain. Phir users ko real-time predictions chahiye hote hain, to online pipeline banayi jati hai. Aakhir me dono pipelines ko unify karne ki koshish hoti hai — ek hi pipeline jo training aur inference dono ke liye features banaye.

Train/serve skew — do pipelines ka khatra

Training aur inference ke liye do alag pipelines rakhna bugs ka common source hai. Training pipeline ek tareeke se features banati hai, inference pipeline doosre tareeke se — aur model ko pata bhi nahi chalta. Example: training me ek feature ka average alag tareeke se compute hua, inference me alag tareeke se — model ki performance silently gir jayegi.

Iska solution hai pipelines ko unify karna: training aur inference ke liye ek hi code, ek hi logic. Online prediction ke liye data pipeline me streaming features, batch features aur model logic — teeno ko saath me design karna padta hai.

Yaad rakho: training aur serving ke beech koi bhi difference — chahe woh feature computation ho, data format ho ya preprocessing ho — skew hai, aur skew silent failures ka sabse bada cause hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 6
← PichhlaBatch prediction vs online predictionAgla →Model compression — chhota model, tez inference
06.4Chapter 6 — Model Deployment

Model compression — chhota model, tez inference

Bade models ko production me, khaas taur par edge devices par, chalana mushkil hota hai. Model compression se model chhota aur tez banta hai, thodi si accuracy ki keemat par.

4 main techniques

  • Low-rank factorization: bade matrices ko chhote matrices ke product se approximate karo. Mobile ke liye banaye gaye ek famous lightweight network ne standard convolution ko depthwise aur pointwise convolution me tod kar parameters bahut kam kar diye.
  • Knowledge distillation: ek bade teacher model se ek chhote student model ko sikhao. Student teacher ki soft predictions se seekhta hai, sirf hard labels se nahi — isliye chhota hone ke bawjood achha perform karta hai.
  • Pruning: model ke un weights ya connections ko hata do jo predictions me zyada contribute nahi karte. Pruned model chhota aur tez hota hai. Lottery ticket hypothesis kehti hai ki dense networks ke andar chhote sub-networks hote hain jo akele train karne par bhi achha perform karte hain.
  • Quantization: weights aur activations ko kam bits me represent karo — jaise 32-bit float ki jagah 8-bit integer. Isse model size 4x kam aur inference tez ho jata hai. Kai frameworks post-training quantization free me dete hain. Quantization-aware training me model ko training ke time hi low precision ke liye prepare kiya jata hai.

Experiments me dikha ki compression methods se latency me bada sudhaar aata hai. Lekin har method ka apna tradeoff hai — compression badhane se accuracy gir sakti hai, isliye har use case ke liye sahi balance dhoondhna chahiye.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 6
← PichhlaBatch se online tak — aur train/serve skewAgla →Cloud vs edge — aur models ko edge ke liye optimize karna
06.5Chapter 6 — Model Deployment

Cloud vs edge — aur models ko edge ke liye optimize karna

Model kahan chalega — cloud server par ya user ke device (edge) par — yeh ek bada architectural decision hai.

Cloud vs edge

  • Cloud: compute unlimited hai, bade models chal sakte hain, update karna aasan hai. Lekin network latency hoti hai, aur data ko device se cloud bhejna padta hai — privacy aur cost dono ke issues hain.
  • Edge: latency bahut kam hoti hai, data device par hi rehta hai (privacy behtar), aur offline bhi kaam karta hai. Lekin compute aur memory limited hain, aur har device par model update karna mushkil hai.
  • Jaise-jaise hardware powerful ho raha hai, models cloud se edge ki taraf move ho rahe hain — pehle online prediction, phir on-device prediction.

Edge ke liye compiling aur optimization

Model code ko machine code me badalne ke liye intermediate representations (IRs) ki series use hoti hai — high-level IR se low-level IR tak, jise "lowering" kehte hain. Har hardware backend (CPU, GPU, TPU) ke alag compute primitives aur memory layouts hote hain.

  • Loop tiling: bade loops ko chhote tiles me todna taaki data cache me fit ho.
  • Operator fusion: kai operators ko ek me mila dena taaki beech ka data memory me likhna-padna na pade. Vertical aur horizontal fusion dono hote hain.
  • Auto-tuning: ek auto-tuner alag-alag optimization strategies try karke sabse tez wali dhoondhta hai — ek experiment me isse ek popular GPU library se bhi zyada speedup mila.

Hardware startups ki bheed bhi badh rahi hai — 2021 tak kai startups ne ML chips ke liye funding uthayi thi. Hardware aur software ka co-design aage ka trend hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 6
← PichhlaModel compression — chhota model, tez inferenceAgla →Model optimization aur ML in browsers
06.6Chapter 6 — Model Deployment

Model optimization aur ML in browsers

Model ko deploy karne ke baad bhi optimization khatm nahi hota. Model optimization ka matlab hai model ko uske deployment environment ke hisaab se tez aur efficient banana.

Model optimization kya hai

Optimization me model ki architecture, precision aur execution plan — teeno ko target hardware ke hisaab se tune kiya jata hai. Yeh kaam optimization engineers karte hain, jinki job descriptions me compilers, hardware aur ML — teeno ki samajh mangi jati hai.

ML se ML ko optimize karna

Ek interesting trend hai: ML ka use karke ML models ko optimize karna — jaise auto-tuners jo best kernel configurations dhoondhte hain, ya learned cost models jo batate hain ki kaunsa optimization sabse tez hoga. Yeh ek naya field hai, lekin tezi se badh raha hai.

ML in browsers

Models ko browser me bhi chalaya ja sakta hai — JavaScript-based ML libraries se. Isse users ko kuch install nahi karna padta, data browser me hi rehta hai, aur demos share karna aasan ho jata hai. Lekin browser me compute limited hota hai, isliye sirf chhote models ya quantized models hi chal sakte hain.

Overall lesson: deployment sirf model ko server par rakhna nahi hai — compression, hardware, optimization aur user experience — sab kuch saath me sochna padta hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 6
← PichhlaCloud vs edge — aur models ko edge ke liye optimize karnaAgla →ML systems kyun fail hote hain — ek kahani se shuruaat
07.1Chapter 7 — Why ML Systems Fail in Production

ML systems kyun fail hote hain — ek kahani se shuruaat

Chapter ki shuruaat ek kahani se hoti hai: ek company ne ek consulting firm se grocery demand predict karne ka model banwaya. Chhe mahine me model bana, deploy hua, aur shuru me performance bahut achhi thi. Company khush thi — woh investors ko bata sakte the ki woh AI-powered hain.

Lekin ek saal baad numbers girne lage. Kuch items ki demand hamesha zyada estimate ho rahi thi — extra items expire ho jate the. Kuch items ki demand hamesha kam estimate ho rahi thi — sales loss ho raha tha. Inventory team pehle manual corrections karti rahi, lekin aakhir me model itna kharab ho gaya ki use karna band karna pada. Company ke paas 3 options the: same firm ko bahut paise dekar update karwayein, doosri firm ko aur zyada paise dein, ya in-house team hire karein.

Lesson

Model deploy karna process ka end nahi hai. Model ki performance time ke saath degrade hoti hai. Deploy karne ke baad bhi performance monitor karni padti hai aur updates deploy karne padte hain. Yahi is chapter aur agle chapter ka topic hai.

Failures ke 3 bade causes

  • Production data training data se alag hai: data distribution badal gaya hai.
  • Edge cases aur outliers: rare cases jinhe model ne training me theek se nahi seekha.
  • Degenerate feedback loops: system ke outputs hi system ke inputs ko influence karne lagte hain.

Pehle do causes data se jude hain, teesra system design se juda hai — aur teesra sabse dangerous hai, kyunki woh training data ke biases ko perpetuate karta hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 7
← PichhlaModel optimization aur ML in browsersAgla →Production data alag kyun hota hai — edge cases aur outliers
07.2Chapter 7 — Why ML Systems Fail in Production

Production data alag kyun hota hai — edge cases aur outliers

Model development me jo data use hota hai, woh production ke data se alag ho sakta hai — aur yeh difference failures ka sabse common cause hai.

Production data differing from training data

Training data carefully collect aur clean kiya jata hai. Production data messy hota hai, usme naye patterns hote hain, aur woh time ke saath badalta hai. Example: ek model ko hospital ke quiet rooms me record ki gayi awaaz par train kiya gaya, lekin jab use phone app me deploy kiya gaya, to recordings me background noise aur alag timings thi — performance gir gayi.

Edge cases

Edge cases woh rare inputs hote hain jo training data me kam ya bilkul nahi hote. Self-driving cars ke liye edge cases — jaise sadak par ek ajeeb object — sabse badi challenge hain. Edge cases ko handle karne ke liye unhe dhoondhna, unka data collect karna, aur model ko un par test karna padta hai.

Outliers

Outliers woh examples hote hain jo baaki data se bahut alag hote hain. Model development me outliers decision boundary ko bigaad sakte hain — ek outlier ki wajah se poori boundary shift ho sakti hai. Kai baar outliers ko hatana faydemand hota hai, kyunki usse model behtar decision boundary seekhta hai. Lekin outliers ko blindly hatana bhi galat hai — kabhi-kabhi outlier hi sabse important signal hota hai, jaise fraud detection me.

Natural labels aur feedback loop bhi yahan judte hain: production me jo labels milte hain (jaise user ne click kiya ya nahi) woh natural labels hote hain, lekin woh biased ho sakte hain — kyunki users ko wohi dikhaya gaya jo model ne recommend kiya tha.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 7
← PichhlaML systems kyun fail hote hain — ek kahani se shuruaatAgla →Degenerate feedback loops — jab model khud ko kharab kare
07.3Chapter 7 — Why ML Systems Fail in Production

Degenerate feedback loops — jab model khud ko kharab kare

Degenerate feedback loop tab hota hai jab system ke outputs wapas system ke inputs ban jate hain, aur har round me bias badhta jata hai. Yeh recommender systems me sabse zyada dikhta hai.

Kaise banta hai loop

Ek music recommendation ka example lo: model ek gaane ko pehle position par dikhata hai, user use click karta hai kyunki woh pehle dikh raha tha, aur system is click ko signal samajh kar gaane ko aur zyada recommend karta hai. Gaana popular isliye nahi hai kyunki woh achha hai — woh popular isliye hai kyunki use pehle dikhaya gaya tha. Har round me yeh bias badhta jata hai, aur diversity khatm ho jati hai.

Detection

Feedback loops ko detect karna mushkil hai, kyunki metrics achhe dikhte hain — clicks badh rahe hain! Lekin clicks badhna isliye hai kyunki system wahi dikha raha hai jo pehle se popular hai. Diversity metrics aur exploration ko track karke loops ka pata lagaya ja sakta hai.

Correction

Ek naive fix: inference ke time "pehle position par tha" wale feature ko False set kar do, taaki model position ke bina predict kare. Lekin yeh kaafi nahi hai. Ek sophisticated approach: do models use karo. Pehla model predict kare ki user recommendation ko dekhega aur consider karega ya nahi (position ko dhyaan me rakh kar). Doosra model predict kare ki dekhne ke baad user click karega ya nahi (position ko ignore karke). Isse position ka bias alag ho jata hai.

Feedback loops ko theek karne ke liye exploration zaroori hai — kabhi-kabhi woh items bhi dikhao jo model ko lagta hai ki popular nahi honge, taaki system naye patterns seekh sake.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 7
← PichhlaProduction data alag kyun hota hai — edge cases aur outliersAgla →Data distribution shifts — covariate, label aur concept drift
07.4Chapter 7 — Why ML Systems Fail in Production

Data distribution shifts — covariate, label aur concept drift

Data distribution shift ka matlab hai: model jis data par train hua tha, uska distribution production ke data se alag ho gaya hai, aur isliye predictions ki accuracy girti jati hai. Training distribution ko source distribution aur inference distribution ko target distribution kehte hain.

Maths — P(X, Y) ke 2 decompositions

Inputs ko X aur outputs ko Y kaho. Joint distribution P(X, Y) ko 2 tareekon se likha ja sakta hai:

  • P(X, Y) = P(Y|X) × P(X)
  • P(X, Y) = P(X|Y) × P(Y)

Inse 3 subtypes define hote hain:

1. Covariate shift — P(X) badla, P(Y|X) wahi

Input distribution badal gaya, lekin ek input ke liye label ki probability wahi hai. Example: breast cancer detection me training data me 40 se zyada umar ki auratein zyada thi, lekin inference data me kam — P(X) badla, lekin ek given age par cancer ki probability wahi hai. Covariate shift sample selection bias se juda hai, aur active learning aur oversampling se bhi ho sakta hai. Agar pata ho ki distribution kaise badlega, to importance weighting se model ko adapt kiya ja sakta hai.

2. Label shift — P(Y) badla, P(X|Y) wahi

Output distribution badal gaya, lekin ek output ke liye input distribution wahi hai. Example: ek preventive dawa se cancer ki probability har age me kam ho gayi — P(Y) badla, lekin cancer wale logon ki age distribution wahi hai. Label shift covariate shift se juda hai, aur dono ke detection methods similar hain.

3. Concept drift — P(Y|X) badla, P(X) wahi

Same input, different output. Example: COVID se pehle San Francisco me 3-bedroom apartment ki keemat 20 lakh dollar thi, COVID ke baad wahi apartment sasta ho gaya — input (apartment features) wahi, lekin price ka relation badal gaya. Yeh sabse mushkil shift hai, kyunki model ka seekha hua mapping hi galat ho gaya hai.

Asliyat me kai baar ek se zyada shifts ek saath hote hain. Research me inke naam ko lekar confusion bhi hai — alag papers same phenomenon ko alag naam dete hain.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 7
← PichhlaDegenerate feedback loops — jab model khud ko kharab kareAgla →Shifts ko detect aur handle karna — retraining hi main solution
07.5Chapter 7 — Why ML Systems Fail in Production

Shifts ko detect aur handle karna — retraining hi main solution

Shift ko detect karna aur use handle karna — dono mushkil hain. Book batati hai ki industry me sabse common solution retraining hai, lekin retraining se pehle detection zaroori hai.

Detection ke tareeke

  • Statistical tests: do distributions ko compare karne ke liye tests use hote hain — jaise ek popular two-sample test, aur density difference estimation par based methods. Kai drift detection algorithms ek open-source library me implement hain.
  • Time window ka dhyaan: shift detect karna time scale par depend karta hai. Agar base distribution ke liye day 9–14 ka data lo, to day 15 shift dikh sakta hai; lekin agar lamba window lo, to shift chhup sakta hai. Chhota window false alarms deta hai, bada window real shifts ko chhupa deta hai.
  • Labels ke bina detection: production me labels milna slow ya mehenga hota hai. Isliye aksar input distribution ko monitor kiya jata hai, labels ka wait kiye bina.
  • Accuracy ko sahi tareeke se track karo: cumulative accuracy sudden dips ko chhupa deti hai — jaise hour 16–18 ke beech accuracy giri, lekin cumulative average me woh dikha nahi. Isliye windowed metrics use karo.

Handling — retraining

Shift ko bina retraining ke handle karna possible ho sakta hai, lekin industry me sabse common solution model ko retrain karna hai — naye data par. Retraining ke liye yeh decide karna padta hai: kab retrain karein, kis data par retrain karein, aur purana model kab replace karein. Yeh decisions agle chapter (Monitoring aur Continual Learning) ka topic hain.

Ek honest note: research community ne abhi tak iska standard narrative nahi banaya hai. Kai studies assume karti hain ki hume pehle se pata hai ki distribution kaise shift hoga, ya dono distributions ke labels mil jayenge — lekin reality me hume future data ke baare me pata nahi hota, aur naye data ke labels lena costly ya infeasible hota hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 7
← PichhlaData distribution shifts — covariate, label aur concept driftAgla →Monitoring aur Continual Learning — overview (Early Release me poora chapter nahi hai)
08.1Chapter 8 — Monitoring and Continual Learning

Monitoring aur Continual Learning — overview (Early Release me poora chapter nahi hai)

Is chapter ka poora content is Early Release PDF me nahi hai — yeh overview book ke cross-references se hai. Chapter 7 ke end me book kehti hai: ML models ka fail hona dhoondhna aasan step hai; mushkil step hai systems ko failures ke liye monitor karna aur changing environments ke hisaab se adapt karna — aur yahi agle chapter ka topic hai: Monitoring aur Continual Learning.

Book ke cross-references se kya pata chalta hai

  • Monitoring: production me model ki performance ko continuously track karna — accuracy, data distributions, latency, aur system health. Shift detection ke tools aur metrics yahan aate hain.
  • Continual learning: model ko naye data se lagatar update karna — users ke feedback se seekhna, aur naye patterns ko adopt karna. Book me kai jagah kaha gaya hai ki continual learning se models ko users ke feedback se behtar banaya ja sakta hai.
  • Contextual bandits: Chapter 7 me kaha gaya hai ki contextual bandits jaise methods item diversity badhane me madad kar sakte hain — yeh bhi isi chapter ka hissa bataya gaya hai.
  • Online learning: Chapter 1 me kaha gaya hai ki bina data ke launch kiye gaye systems online learning se seekh sakte hain — yeh bhi continual learning se juda hai.

Yeh overview sirf isliye diya gaya hai taaki tumhe pata chale ki story aage kahan jati hai. Poora detail — monitoring ke metrics, retraining strategies, aur continual learning ke methods — is Early Release PDF me available nahi hai, isliye yahan koi detail invent nahi ki gayi hai.

Source: Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly, Chapter 8
